Analyte-name aliases

Source: R/aliases.R
analyte_aliases.Rd

The mapping from the analyte names used by sampleTidy (and other upstream stores) to the names hydroSense computes with. add_lmf(), to_meq(), add_mspaf() and mspaf_pipeline() apply it to their inputs, so data stored under either spelling is accepted, and return the caller's rows with their original names.

Usage

analyte_aliases()

Value

A data frame with character columns alias (an upstream name) and canonical (the hydroSense name), one row per alias. Names that already match map to themselves.

Details

Two upstream quantities have no hydroSense counterpart of their own and map to themselves: "Alkalinity-total-CaCO3" (the sum of "CO3-CaCO3" and "HCO3-CaCO3") and "NO2+NO3-N" (the sum of "NO3-N" and "NO2-N"). add_lmf() uses such a combined value in place of its two species, and ignores it when the species themselves are present, so nothing is counted twice.

Examples

analyte_aliases()
#> # A tibble: 21 × 2
#>    alias canonical
#>    <chr> <chr>    
#>  1 Na    Na       
#>  2 K     K        
#>  3 Ca    Ca       
#>  4 Mg    Mg       
#>  5 Cl    Cl       
#>  6 SO4²⁻ SO4²⁻    
#>  7 F     F        
#>  8 NH3-N NH3-N    
#>  9 NO3-N NO3-N    
#> 10 NO2-N NO2-N    
#> # ℹ 11 more rows
